      "id": "AMLO-2022-5B-001",
      "type": "observed_fact",
      "claim": "The update note states that this version of the biography was published on 29 November 2018; López Obrador's presidential term ran from 1 December 2018 to 1 October 2024; and his successor was Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, former head of government of Mexico City and winner of the 2 June 2024 presidential election for the governing MORENA party and the Sigamos Haciendo Historia coalition.",

    },
    {
      "id": "AMLO-2022-5B-002",
      "type": "author_assertion",
      "claim": "The biography describes López Obrador as the first Mexican president considered clearly left-wing and states that he began his term on 1 December 2018 with his coalition holding an absolute majority in both chambers of Congress, amid gestures renouncing some costly attributes of the presidency.",
      "locator": "Extracted HTML block 6, paragraph beginning “El 1 de diciembre de 2018”"
    },
    {
      "id": "AMLO-2022-5B-003",
      "type": "author_assertion",
      "claim": "The 2018 electoral program emphasized “austeridad republicana,” defined as redirecting public resources from current expenditure to investment without raising taxes; combating poverty and improving human development among vulnerable groups; gradual withdrawal of the Armed Forces from internal-security missions, with a goal of “pacifying” Mexico in three years; increasing domestically produced gasoline supply; energy and food self-sufficiency, including guaranteed prices for local agricultural producers; “erradicación” of political corruption by “dando ejemplo” from Los Pinos; and firm defense of Mexican migrants.",
      "locator": "Extracted HTML block 5, paragraph beginning “El programa electoral incidía”"
    },
    {
      "id": "AMLO-2022-5B-004",
      "type": "author_assertion",
      "claim": "The biography says the 2018–2024 platform suggested a “socialdemocracia pragmática” that accepted free markets, macroeconomic stability, budgetary discipline, and a floating peso, while rejecting privatizing tendencies and the foreign control of strategic sectors and prioritizing national production.",
      "locator": "Extracted HTML block 6, first paragraph"
    },
    {
      "id": "AMLO-2022-5B-005",
      "type": "author_assertion",
      "claim": "López Obrador promised to “hacer justicia sin venganza ni odio” when ending corruption and former presidents’ privileges and stated, “no voy a meter a Peña Nieto en la cárcel.”",
      "locator": "Extracted HTML block 6, second paragraph"
    },
    {
      "id": "AMLO-2022-5B-006",
      "type": "author_assertion",
      "claim": "Before taking office, López Obrador called for discussion of a “Constitución Moral” intended to guide Mexico’s “Cuarta Transformación,” celebrated the results of the Consulta Nacional Ciudadana on the incoming administration’s priority programs, and presented a Plan Nacional de Paz y Seguridad that included creating a Guardia Nacional to relieve the Army and addressed “amnistía condicionada” for drug traffickers. The incoming government team was also studying decriminalization of the consumption of soft drugs.",
      "locator": "Extracted HTML block 6, paragraph beginning “El 1 de diciembre de 2018,” final two sentences"
    },
    {
      "id": "AMLO-2022-5B-007",
      "type": "author_assertion",
      "claim": "The biography states that López Obrador considered the USMCA beneficial; that in October 2018 he spoke of offering work visas to Central American migrants; and that on 26 November, after an attempted assault repelled with tear gas by U.S. police, Trump threatened to close the border “permanentemente.”",
      "locator": "Extracted HTML block 7, first and second paragraphs"
    },
    {
      "id": "AMLO-2022-5B-008",
      "type": "author_assertion",
      "claim": "During López Obrador’s government of the Federal District, the city undertook a vigorous public-works campaign and provided social-protection programs, most notably the Pensión Universal Alimenticia para Adultos Mayores. The municipal government resisted implementing Seguro Popular, arguing that Federal District residents already received the necessary social coverage free of charge from municipal institutions.",
      "locator": "Extracted HTML block 21, first paragraph"
    },
    {
      "id": "AMLO-2022-5B-009",
      "type": "author_assertion",
      "claim": "According to the opposition, principally the PAN, López Obrador’s administration squandered the Federal District budget through populist spending without concern for debts.       "locator": "Extracted HTML block 21, second paragraph"
    },

      "id": "AMLO-2022-5B-010",
      "type": "author_assertion",
      "claim": "The 2006 coalition program called for ending “privilegios,” “corrupción,” and “saqueo,” sweeping corruption “de arriba para abajo,” cutting the president’s salary in half, and investigating FOBAPROA through a Comisión de la Verdad.     },
    {
      "id": "AMLO-2022-5B-011",
      "type": "author_assertion",
      "claim": "The 2006 program ruled out any process leading to even partial privatization of Pemex; defended every worker’s constitutional right to a “justo” and “digno” salary without specifying an amount; called for adding a development-cooperation chapter and protections for domestic agricultural producers to NAFTA; and stated that migration could not be resolved “con muros ni con la militarización fronteriza.”",
      "locator": "Extracted HTML block 31, second and third paragraphs"
    },
    {
      "id": "AMLO-2022-5B-012",
      "type": "author_assertion",
      "claim": "In López Obrador’s book “Fobaproa, expediente abierto: reseña y archivo,” he described the fund’s conduct as openly unconstitutional and as the “fraude más grande de la historia después de La Conquista.”",
      "locator": "Extracted HTML block 17, second paragraph"
    },

      "type": "interpretation",
      "claim": "The author frames López Obrador’s 2018 victory as the debut in Mexico’s government of a party alternative with a short history in opposition and describes his 2018–2024 platform as suggesting a “socialdemocracia pragmática.”",

      "type": "interpretation",
      "claim": "The biography contrasts supporters’ portrayal of López Obrador as “voluntarioso y esforzado,” committed to social causes and citizens’ welfare, austere, transparent, and participatory, with adversaries’ descriptions of him as an “extremista” and “populista”; it also reports Enrique Krauze’s label “mesías tropical.”",

      "type": "author_assertion",
      "claim": "The biography states that López Obrador’s 6 a.m. press conferences, popularly known as “las mañaneras,” generated unusual journalistic interest and “marcaron la agenda política del país.”",

      "type": "unresolved_allegation",
      "claim": "In the 2004 “videoescándalo,” recordings showed Gustavo Ponce Meléndez, René Bejarano Martínez, and Carlos Ímaz Gispert in compromising situations involving Carlos Ahumada Kurtz. The biography says it was objectively difficult to imagine that López Obrador was unaware of the dealings of someone as close to him as Bejarano, but also states that the scandal did not implicate López Obrador to the point of endangering his institutional position. On 4 May, the new attorney general, Daniel Cabeza de Vaca, announced that the Public Ministry was withdrawing the charges and closing the case.",

## VERIFIED ADDITIONS

None.

## REOPEN REQUESTS

- Reopen any claim about **2022 measured performance, implementation, legal status, beneficiaries, incidence, or crisis response** using post-2018 sources. The supplied extract does not support such claims.
- Reopen the draft’s suggestion that the biography reports institutional rejection of AMLO’s fraud claims across **“2006–2018.”** The extract supports election-monitoring and tribunal conclusions for **2006**, but not that broader time span.
